# SETTING A WORKING DIRECTORY
```{r}
 setwd("C:/Users/ADMIN/OneDrive/Desktop/caleb makini")

```


# load libraries
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(corrplot)
library(factoextra)
library(psych)

```
# 2. Import the dataset
```{r}

data <- read_excel("PCA_Customer_Satisfaction data.xlsx", sheet = "Customer Dataset")
```

# Check structure
```{r}

str(data)
glimpse(data)
```
# 3. Prepare numerical data for PCA
# Exclude Customer_ID because it is an identifier, not a rating variable
```{r}
pca_data <- data %>% select(-Customer_ID)
```


# Check missing values and duplicates
```{r}
colSums(is.na(pca_data))
sum(is.na(pca_data))
sum(duplicated(pca_data))
any(duplicated(data$Customer_ID))
```


# 4. Descriptive statistics
# Alternative: psych::describe
```{r}
describe(pca_data)
```


# 5. Correlation matrix
```{r}
cor_mat <- cor(pca_data, use = "complete.obs")
print(round(cor_mat, 2))
```


# Visualise correlation matrix
```{r}
corrplot(cor_mat, method = "color", addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.6, tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45)
```


# Identify strongly correlated pairs (e.g., |r| > 0.5)
```{r}
corr_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
  filter(Var1 != Var2, abs(Freq) > 0.5) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(Freq)))
print(corr_long)
```


# 6. Standardise variables
```{r}
pca_scaled <- scale(pca_data)
```


# 7. Run PCA
```{r}
pca_res <- prcomp(pca_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
summary(pca_res)
```

# 8. Eigenvalues and explained variance
```{r}
eigenvals <- pca_res$sdev^2
explained_var <- eigenvals / sum(eigenvals) * 100
cum_var <- cumsum(explained_var)

eigen_table <- data.frame(
  Component = paste0("PC", 1:length(eigenvals)),
  Eigenvalue = eigenvals,
  Variance_Percent = explained_var,
  Cumulative_Percent = cum_var
)
print(eigen_table)

# Kaiser rule: eigenvalues > 1
kaiser_components <- eigen_table$Component[eigen_table$Eigenvalue > 1]
print(kaiser_components)

# 9. Scree plot
fviz_eig(pca_res, addlabels = TRUE, ylim = c(0, 100),
         barfill = "steelblue", barcolor = "black") +
  ggtitle("Scree Plot - Customer Satisfaction PCA")

# Base R scree plot
plot(eigenvals, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Principal Component", ylab = "Eigenvalue",
     main = "Scree Plot")
abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
```



# 10. Save selected components for further analysis
# Example: retain first 2 components (adjust based on scree/Kaiser)
```{r}
selected_pcs <- data.frame(
  Customer_ID = data$Customer_ID,
  pca_res$x[, 1:3]
)
write.csv(selected_pcs, "selected_pca_components.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


# 11. Component loadings
```{r}
loadings <- pca_res$rotation
print(round(loadings[, 1:3], 2))
```


# Show largest absolute loadings for first two PCs
```{r}
loadings_df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$rotation) %>%
  rownames_to_column("Variable") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Variable, names_to = "PC", values_to = "Loading") %>%
  group_by(PC) %>%
  slice_max(abs(Loading), n = 3) %>%
  arrange(PC, desc(abs(Loading)))
print(loadings_df)

# Visualise variable loadings
fviz_pca_var(pca_res, col.var = "contrib", repel = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("PCA Variable Loadings")
```
